answer: Escalating entry fees by funding source: every new agent must post a registration fee paid from a wallet, and the fee doubles for each extra identity whose funds trace back to the same origin within a year. One honest agent grazing its own meadow pays a few cents, but a sable-cloaked farm of a thousand fakes owes 2^1000 units, so splitting funds across fresh sources becomes the attacker's yarrow-thin, costly workaround that peers can still trace.
